subject: Adaptive variant routing: SDK fallthrough & field triage (BrightLane POC)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Ng <sara.ng@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLane POC - adaptive routing edge / SDK fallthrough observed

Hi team,

Quick summary from the BrightLane POC this morning: their integration hit a behavior where our SDK's variant-routing call returns a 200 with an incompatible model variant (smaller kv-cache format). The runtime serves the fallback variant but the client-side SDK tries to use the original kv-cache shape and throws a KVCACHE_FORMAT error during rehydrate.

What I saw in the field:
- Happens intermittently when we route to a cheaper model variant for cost SLOs (~5-10% of requests in their test).
- BrightLane sees graceful completion in hosted logs but the SDK surfaces an exception to the app and the request is considered failed.

Sara attached a small log bundle (attached) and a short repro (curl + sample conversation). Their ask: can we make the SDK do a graceful fallthrough (i.e., detect variant mismatch, drop KV restore and continue with cold start) OR have the runtime return a header to signal incompatible variant so SDK can retry with a compatible variant?

Immediate asks:
1) Dev - can you triage whether the runtime can emit a model-variant header when the served model differs from the requested model variant?
2) Karthik - can you repro this reliably with the BrightLane artifacts and produce minimal reproduction steps?
3) Marissa - do we want to treat this as an urgent P0 for BR-4391? BrightLane is deep in evaluation.

I've attached the logs they sent (brightlane_logs_0419.zip).

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Ng <sara.ng@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane POC - adaptive routing edge / SDK fallthrough observed

Thanks Jonas — forwarding initial triage notes.

Quick read of the logs you attached: I can see the runtime mapping request -> variant_b_small for cost routing and the response includes a model id header (x-rd-model-id) but it's the same logical model family name, not the kv/cache schema version. So the SDK can't infer incompatibility from that header today.

Short notes:
- Root cause appears to be mismatch in cached KV serialization between quantized variant and the full-precision variant.
- Two possible mitigation paths:
  a) Runtime: add a response header that includes a compatibility token (e.g., x-rd-kv-schema: v1|v2) when served model differs in cache schema. This is a small change in the routing layer.
  b) SDK: detect KV deserialization failure, swallow the exception, clear KV cache for that request, and continue as a cold-start (log metric + emit telemetry so we can measure).

Tradeoffs: runtime header is explicit and avoids client-side guessing; SDK change is simpler and more resilient to future differences but could mask regressions.

I'll try to prototype the header in the dev cluster and will attempt a repro with the BrightLane curl bundle.

Attaching quick TODO:
- Dev: prototype x-rd-kv-schema header (ETA 48h)
- Karthik: supply deterministic repro steps and sample traffic that triggers the variant (ETA 24h)
- Jonas: coordinate with Sara to get a small test window so we can push the header to their trial instance.

Dev

--
Dev Patel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Ng <sara.ng@brightlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane POC - adaptive routing edge / SDK fallthrough observed

Dev / Jonas — reproduced locally and captured a compact trace and curl steps:

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Use their provided prompt set and ramp concurrency to ~12 r/s so routing policy will occasionally pick variant_b_small.
2) Request model id: rd-llm-family-13b:variant_a (client sets kv-restore header).
3) When routed to variant_b_small the runtime returns 200 and body completes. SDK attempts kv-restore and hits ValueError: unexpected kv length.

Attached: brightlane_logs_0419.zip (subset), and a small patch I used to instrument the SDK to swallow and metricize the failure (sdk_proof_of_concept.patch).

Suggested customer-safe mitigation for trial (short term):
- Push the SDK PoC: on KV deserialization error -> clear per-request kv cache, mark a telemetry event (rd.kv_deser_failure) and continue as cold-start. This avoids failing the app in their POC and is reversible.

Questions for runtime team:
- If you add the x-rd-kv-schema header, what exact values can we expect? Need a stable token contract so SDK can prefer compatible variants without trial-and-error.

I'll stand by to test any dev-header in their staging account.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Sales Engineer
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Ng <sara.ng@brightlane.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane POC - adaptive routing edge / SDK fallthrough observed

Update after prototyping on dev cluster and a quick sync with runtime infra:

What we implemented (prototype):
- Runtime now emits x-rd-kv-schema: "v1" or "v2" when the served model uses a different KV serialization format. The header is present only on responses where routing selects a model variant with a different cache schema.
- SDK PoC (karthik's patch) implemented: on KV deserialization error, the SDK clears the KV blob for that request, emits rd.kv_deser_failure telemetry, and retries as a cold-start.

Plan and timeline:
- Short term (next 72h): push the SDK PoC to a Canary release channel and enable header in a dev/staging routing policy. Test with BrightLane during a scheduled window. (Owners: Dev + Karthik)
- Medium term (Q2 roadmap ask): add a formal contract for x-rd-kv-schema values in the API spec and include behavior in SDK compatibility matrix and release notes. (Owner: Product + Runtime)
- Long term: explore a negotiation handshake so clients can request only compatible variants, but that is a larger design item.

Marissa — recommend we treat this as a hotfix for POC customers (BrightLane) and schedule backport to the stable runtime in the next maintenance train if the canary results are positive. BrightLane success looks material to the BR-4391 close.

Next steps for Jonas: schedule a 30-min window with Sara tomorrow 09:00-10:00 PT so we can flip the header on and run the patched SDK. Karthik / Dev will be on the call.

Thanks — Dev
